description: The pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the proportional distribution of media outlets contributing to a dataset or analysis, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet and its relative share. The chart contains 18 distinct slices, each labeled with the name of a media organization and accompanied by a numerical value indicating its percentage or count within the total. The largest segment is “Breitbart,” occupying 14% of the chart and rendered in a prominent blue hue. The second-largest is “Other,” at 13%, shown in gray. “Drudge Report” and “The Daily Caller” each account for 8%, colored orange and green respectively. “NPR” and “Vox” each represent 6%, in purple and brown. “The Guardian” and “BBC” each hold 5%, in pink and dark gray. Smaller segments include “RT,” “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Daily Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” and “CNN,” each at 3%, displayed in various colors including yellow, teal, red, and magenta. “Shareblue” and “PoliticusUSA” also appear at 3%. The chart uses a standard radial layout with slices radiating from the center, and all labels and values are positioned outside the pie with lines connecting them to their respective segments. No slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size and color coding. The legend is integrated directly into the chart via labeled pointers, and no additional annotations or explanatory text are present beyond the outlet names and their numerical values.
